metaTitle: Agricultural Land Ceiling Rules for NRBs in Bangladesh
title: Agricultural Land Ceiling Rules for NRBs in Bangladesh
metaDescription: Understand the 60-bigha agricultural land ceiling under the Land Reforms Act 2023 in Bangladesh, inheritance exemptions for NRBs, and legal compliance.
heroIntro: Under Section 4 of the Land Reforms Act, 2023 (Bhumi Sangskar Ain, 2023), no family or individual in Bangladesh may own more than 60 standard bighas (approximately 19.8 acres) of agricultural land, with limited exemptions for inherited property, tea estates, and approved agro-industries. Non-Resident Bangladeshis (NRBs) buying or inheriting farmland must verify total family holdings before Sub-Registry registration.

quickAnswer.heading: At a Glance: Bangladesh Land Ceiling Law
points: Primary Statute: Land Reforms Act, 2023 (Section 4) & State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (Section 90).
Maximum Limit: 60 standard bighas (approx. 1,980 decimals) per family for agricultural land.
Non-Agricultural Land: Residential flats, commercial plots, and urban housing are excluded from the 60-bigha cap.
Penalty for Excess: Land held above the statutory ceiling without government exemption vests in the State.

sections.h2: What Is the 60-Bigha Agricultural Land Ceiling?
sections.content:
Section 4 of the Land Reforms Act, 2023 replaces the older 1984 ordinance and restricts any malik (owner) or family from acquiring or retaining more than 60 standard bighas of agricultural land across Bangladesh. Previously, Section 90 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 set a 100-bigha limit, which was later lowered to 60 bighas to prevent excessive land concentration.

Importantly, the ceiling applies strictly to agricultural (Krishi) land recorded as Nal, Chala, Boro, or Aman in CS/SA/RS/BS Khatians—not to urban residential plots in Dhaka, Chattogram, or Sylhet, nor to apartment units. However, if an NRB purchases rural agricultural parcels in multiple districts, the Sub-Registrar aggregates holdings across the entire country.

Before purchasing any rural parcel, NRBs should verify the land classification through our guide on checking Bangladesh land ownership online and review our NRB land purchase checklist.

sections.h2: How 'Family' Is Defined Under the Land Reforms Act, 2023
sections.content:
Under Section 2 of the Land Reforms Act, 2023, a 'family' includes the owner, their spouse, unmarried sons and daughters, and any dependent parents—meaning separate deeds in a spouse's name do not bypass the 60-bigha limit. Married adult children who maintain independent households are treated as separate family units for ceiling calculation.

When registering a Saf Kabala (sale deed) at the Sub-Registry office under the Registration Act, 1908, the buyer must sign a statutory declaration confirming that the newly acquired agricultural land, combined with existing family holdings, does not exceed 60 bighas. Making a false declaration renders the excess transfer void and exposes the property to forfeiture by the Deputy Commissioner.

For families holding joint ancestral estates, filing a timely partition suit (Batwara) or registering a Heba gift deed can clarify individual shares before mutation.

sections.h2: Exemptions for NRB Inheritance and Commercial Projects
sections.content:
Section 4(2) of the Land Reforms Act, 2023 carves out specific exceptions where holdings above 60 bighas are permitted, including agricultural land acquired strictly by inheritance, approved cooperative societies, tea or rubber plantations, and export-oriented agro-processing industries.

Scenario60-Bigha Cap Applies?Statutory Basis & Condition
New Purchase of Agricultural LandYes (Strict 60-bigha cap)Section 4(1), Land Reforms Act, 2023; excess vests in Government.
Inherited Ancestral FarmlandExempt (subject to rules)Section 4(2); heirs may retain inherited land subject to statutory reporting.
Urban Residential / Commercial PlotNoApplies only to agricultural land; non-agricultural plots are outside the cap.
Approved Agro-Industrial ProjectExempt with Govt. ApprovalRequires prior Land Ministry clearance and project use compliance.

NRBs who hold dual citizenship should also confirm eligibility rules in our article on dual citizen property ownership in Bangladesh, or consult a land lawyer in Bangladesh if inherited land is encroached upon.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Compliance Before Buying Farmland from Abroad
sections.content:
NRBs purchasing rural or semi-urban land should complete a five-step title and ceiling audit before remitting purchase funds to Bangladesh.

  1. Audit Existing Family Khatians: Collect CS, SA, RS, and BS Khatians held by you, your spouse, and minor children to calculate total existing decimals (1 bigha = 33 decimals).
  2. Verify Land Classification: Check the latest BS/RS Porcha and Mouza map to confirm whether the plot is classified as agricultural (Krishi) or homestead/commercial (Vita/Bastu).
  3. Execute Embassy-Attested Power of Attorney: If you cannot travel to Dhaka, appoint a trusted representative via an Embassy-attested Power of Attorney for Bangladesh property.
  4. Complete Sub-Registry & e-Mutation: Submit the ceiling declaration at registration and complete e-Mutation (Namjari) with the AC (Land) office.
  5. Consult Legal Counsel for High-Value Deals: Engage Advocate Md. Shah Alam for a formal Talashi search and written chain-of-title opinion before signing any Bayna agreement.

sections.h2: Documents Checklist for NRB Land Acquisition
sections.content:
To register agricultural or mixed-use land smoothly and pass AC (Land) mutation scrutiny, prepare the following verified records.

  • Certified copies of CS, SA, RS, and BS Khatians (Porcha) and Mouza map extract.
  • Complete chain of Bia (prior) deeds for at least 25 years and up-to-date Khajna (land development tax) receipts.
  • Non-encumbrance certificate (NEC) / Talashi report from the local Sub-Registry office.
  • Signed statutory declaration of total family agricultural land under Section 4 of the Land Reforms Act, 2023.
  • Bangladeshi NID or NVR-endorsed passport and bank remittance channel proof for NRB buyers.

If you face a boundary dispute, forged deed, or illegal occupation, review NRB legal remedies against land grabbing, visit our NRB Legal Help Desk, or contact our chamber for a free initial consultation.

faqs.question: How many decimals or acres equal 60 bighas in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Under Bangladeshi statutory land measurement, 1 standard bigha equals 33 decimals (approximately 0.33 acres). Therefore, the 60-bigha ceiling under the Land Reforms Act, 2023 equals 1,980 decimals, or roughly 19.8 acres (8.01 hectares) of agricultural land per family.

faqs.question: Does the 60-bigha ceiling apply to residential plots in Dhaka or Uttara?
faqs.answer: No. The ceiling under Section 4 of the Land Reforms Act, 2023 applies exclusively to agricultural (Krishi) land. Residential plots, apartments, and commercial buildings in Dhaka, Chattogram, or other municipal areas are not counted toward the 60-bigha agricultural limit.

faqs.question: What happens if an NRB inherits more than 60 bighas of ancestral farmland?
faqs.answer: Agricultural land acquired strictly through lawful inheritance is generally exempt under Section 4(2) of the Land Reforms Act, 2023. However, once a family already holds 60 bighas or more, it cannot purchase additional agricultural land in Bangladesh without specific government exemption.

faqs.question: Can an NRB convert agricultural land into residential or commercial land?
faqs.answer: Changing land classification from agricultural to non-agricultural requires prior permission from the Deputy Commissioner (DC) under the Land Reforms Act, 2023 and applicable municipal zoning rules such as RAJUK. Unauthorised conversion of fertile agricultural land is an offence.

faqs.question: Can a dual citizen with a foreign passport still own inherited land in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Yes. Bangladeshi citizens holding dual citizenship (with No Visa Required / NVR endorsement) retain full rights to inherit, own, and sell property in Bangladesh. Foreign nationals without Bangladeshi citizenship face strict statutory restrictions on acquiring land.
